_doc: Feature flags (scripts/ops/feature_flags.gd). Overrides: user://feature_flags.json {"name": bool} (ignored when GRIDFALL_FLAGS_IGNORE_USER=1), then env GRIDFALL_FLAGS="overview=0,analytics=1". First-person features use their registry id from scripts/fp/fp_features.gd; FpMode skips a disabled one.

web_shader_warmup.description: Web only: while the loader veil is up, draw one tiny copy of every distinct material the scene uses (scripts/fp/warmup/) so the browser links their shader programs behind the veil instead of mid-play (the Compatibility renderer links each program synchronously at first use: 37 ms median, up to 213 ms, and a new material or the lamps coming on stalled play for 0.4 to 1 s). Measured on a new city: the veil drops 2.8 to 3.6 s later (a 3 s budget checked between batches, so a batch can overshoot; 8.5 s later with a 6 s budget) and frames over 100 ms in the first 90 s fall by 15 to 28% (two sets of 3 to 5 runs), not by half. A grown city (more than 600 distinct materials) is not warmed with warmup_orbit_variants off: it cost 0.8 to 2.1 s and removed no hitch; with it on (default) materials are grouped by shader variant and a grown city is warmed too. It stops at once if the loader's veil is already gone. Progress is shown as Preparing graphics in the loader. Off: nothing is warmed and programs link at first use, as before.

orbit_tree_chunks.description: The Planner (orbit) view plants its trees in 16-tile chunks instead of 48-tile ones, so the renderer culls the forest to what the view and the sun's shadow cascades reach: every chunk the view touched drew all its trees (a grown city's 266k trees are 24 M vertices a frame, and again in each cascade). Same trees in the same places, and the same full-tree / stand-in switch per 48-tile cell (scripts/world/orbit_tree_lod.gd), so the forest looks as it did at every zoom. Cuts vertices and GPU time, not draw calls or the frame interval on a main-thread-bound machine; it adds scene nodes (2,352 tree layers for 300). Off: the 48-tile chunks, as before.

hero_wade.description: The hero can wade into rivers and lakes: the river bed is a gentler 4 m shelf and the hero walks on it up to 0.8 m of water, slower the deeper it gets (no sprint past 0.3 m, a weaker jump), with wet steps and a splash; deeper water is still a limit (a "Too deep to wade" notice). Off: water is a wall again for the hero, as for everyone else (NPCs, cars, animals and thrown bodies never wade). The bed mesh changes shape either way.

ground_profile.description: One table of ground heights (scripts/fp/world/ground_profile.gd) behind both the meshes and the collision, so the height under the hero's feet is the height of the surface he sees: a lot's slab is a true 8 cm step 0.6 m inside its tile edge (not a flat slab across the whole tile eased down at the edge), the apron in front of a lot climbs to the sidewalk exactly as its mesh does, rubble is a slab of its own size. The interim soft step is gone. Everyone who asks the CollisionWorld for ground (the hero, walkers, cars, animals, thrown bodies) sees it. Off: the old flat-tile heights with the soft step, as before.

ground_foot_fit.description: The third-person hero's feet are put on the ground under them (scripts/fp/player/foot_fit.gd): after the animation the pelvis is lowered to the lower foot and a two-bone leg solve plants each foot ON the surface under it, so on a kerb, a lot edge, an apron, a slope or a low wall a leg no longer goes into the concrete or hangs over it. A handful of height samples a frame, smoothed, nothing allocated on flat ground. Off while driving, climbing, knocked down, wading or in first person. Off: the hero's one height for the whole body, as before.

surface_feel.description: Each ground surface feels like itself: footsteps get a level and a pitch of their own (a hard click on asphalt and concrete, soft on grass, a crunch on gravel, a hollow knock on a bridge, damp and low on the sand of a river bank), sand, dirt tracks and gravel are a few per cent slower to run on (soft sand most) and a sprint across dry sand, dirt or gravel kicks up a small puff of dust. Pavement stays full speed. Off: one step level and pitch for every surface, full speed everywhere, no dust, as before.

pack_status.description: Web split builds: the compact background-pack status line in the orbit and first-person HUDs ("Loading city detail · N/M packs", "Some city detail is unavailable" + Retry). It stays hidden on unsplit builds and once every pack is mounted. Off: no status line; downloads still run.

web_split_packs.description: Web only: stream the optional background packs (midlod, sky, traffic, people, props, wildlife, posters, audio) after the playable boot instead of shipping them in it. Needs a split export; on an unsplit build the flag changes nothing. A split build with the flag off is a configuration error, not a rollback: roll back with the unsplit release.

web_sliced_planner.description: Web only: the Planner (orbit view) keeps the time-sliced sim ticks that first person turned on, with a per-frame budget that grows with the speed buttons (4 ms at 1x to 16 ms at 8x), instead of whole ticks that stalled the page 450-670 ms on a grown city. Off: the desktop behaviour on the web too (whole ticks, full speed, stalls).

autosave_gap.description: A morning autosave less than 60 s of wall clock after the last autosave waits until the gap has passed (the Planner's 12 s game days made a 100 ms save every day). Quit and manual saves always go through. Off: every morning autosaves at once, as before.

sim_perf.description: First-person feature: time-sliced sim ticks so growth ticks never freeze the street (slice F).

streetscape.description: First-person feature: street-level light profile, weather and street lights (slice G1).

render_opt.description: First-person feature: quality preset application (including the SSAO switch that goes with the 3D scale), LOD ranges and far-building chunks (slice G2).

web_quality.description: Web quality tier below Low (quality.gd): density caps on traffic, crowd, animals and the rain emitter's streaks (every preset draws the same count there; Low, Medium and High would otherwise draw 800, 1600 and 3000 thicker streaks) and the rain emitter off while the Tab overview is open or the camera is more than 10 m above the player's feet, then tighter 3D scaling, shadows and ranges on the browser build. Auto-applied on the web; desktop runs are untouched. Off: the web build runs the plain Low preset. Trade-off, flag on or off: the first-person view has no SSAO (ambient occlusion, so less contact shading) wherever Compatibility renders the 3D view below native size, which is every preset in the web tier and, with the flag off, web Low (0.77); render_opt applies it with the scale. Scaled SSAO there prints dark horizontal lines on flat ground (rms of the plaza row profile measured on the web build over two plaza boxes: 10 to 14 grey levels with SSAO, 0.7 to 3.0 without); see quality.ssao_ok.

web_real_time_pace.description: Web only: let the browser build keep the world at real-time speed when it runs below 30 fps. Off (default) caps the engine to 2 physics catch-up steps per frame, so below 30 fps every system runs in slow motion (about 80% speed at a grown city's 42 ms frames). On raises the cap to 4 (real time down to 15 fps), at the price of more mayor turns, chat drips and live GMI calls per real minute (about 1.3-2x on a grown city). The player can flip it in the pause menu (Display) and the planner HUD; the choice is saved in user://feature_flags.json.

traffic.description: First-person feature: lane traffic, buses and walking residents (slice E).

cyclists.description: People on bicycles. A quarter of the residents (more of the adventurous and thrifty) keep a bicycle and ride it instead of driving on trips of up to 16 road tiles, and about one in six of the unnamed vehicles in the street is a cyclist. Off: only residents whose day's plan says bike ride, and the street traffic is all motor vehicles.

road_grades.description: Gravel roads, dirt tracks and grass trails. A road order may ask for a cheaper grade, which costs less to build and keep up but is slower to drive and only carries low-density lots; a better grade over an existing road resurfaces it. On foot they have no curbs or street furniture, and the car grips them less. Off: every road order builds a paved street.

interact.description: First-person feature: interaction with residents, buildings, posters and cars (slice A).

hud_widgets.description: First-person feature: minimap, full map, compass and waypoint widgets (slice B).

chat.description: First-person feature: city chat feed, talk dialog and /mayor decrees (slice C).

posters.description: First-person feature: campaign, newspaper, shop and notice posters (slice D).

audio.description: First-person feature: street sound: buses, positional emitters and ambience (slice I).

overview.description: First-person feature: Tab city overview to watch construction sites.

first_day_opening.description: Day 1 of a fresh city a player starts on foot (the first launch and New city in the pause menu; not a loaded save or Continue, which keep their own sky, clock and the ordinary mayor schedule, and not tools or tests; a Planner view round trip on day 1 keeps the clear sky): the sky is clear all day (the daily weather draw is skipped on day 1), the street clock opens at 07:30 instead of 06:00 (CitySim.start_at_progress; tools keep 06:00), the five founding mayor turns land within about 3.5 minutes at 1x instead of spreading over the whole day (replay-cache keys are by day, so recorded answers are unchanged), and the hero spawns facing down the avenue with City Hall at 45 degrees instead of facing the wall. The night look and the quality presets are not touched. Off: day 1 starts at 06:00 in the day's own weather, the mayors spread over the day and the hero faces City Hall, as before.

coach_card.description: First-person feature: the first-minute guidance. A fresh city's welcome toast is replaced by a bottom-centre key-cap card (WASD walk, Shift run, Tab city overview, J AI feed, E talk, Enter chat, Esc menu) that stays 15 seconds or until J, Tab or E (or another first action), and never shows again once the coach_seen setting is saved. A Click to look around pill shows while the pointer is free (not headless, not paused, no menu). One-line hints follow, each once: the first AI decision (J reads it), the first resident within 3 m (E to talk), 60 seconds without input at 1x (] speeds time up) and the first Tab (Planner view button: the full city builder). Off: the one-line welcome toast, no pill, no hints.

drive.description: First-person feature: get into parked or stopped cars with F and drive them.

car_doors.description: Getting into and out of cars the long way: the hero walks round to the driver's door, opens it (coming to rest against anyone on foot stood in its swing rather than through them), climbs in and shuts it (and the reverse, once the car has stopped). Off: F gets in and out at once.

carjack.description: Taking a car with someone at the wheel: F by a car stopped or crawling in traffic holds it while the hero walks to the driver's door, opens it, takes hold of the driver and pulls them out (they go down, get up, shout and run off; a resident walks on to where they were going), then climbs in. The car is never taken without that grab: with no spot beside the door to stand at, or no way to it, the car is let go and the driver stays at the wheel (the hero says "Can't get to the door"), and a driver not yet drawn at the wheel (the people cap, an avatar still loading) is drawn for the hero first, the door waiting up to 1.5 s for it. A driver with no sidewalk near to run for (a bridge, a track) is put down on the road and walks to the shoulder, never deleted. Buses, garbage and delivery trucks (heavy_motors) and bicycle and scooter riders (bike_ride, scooters) are pulled out the same way: they have no door that opens, so the hero reaches in from the side, steps in beside the seat and takes the wheel (or the saddle) once they are out (a bus or truck has no door art: its driver comes out over the cab's low side). The driver and those who saw it remember it and the police are called. Off: only an ambient car can be taken from traffic, its driver simply gone.

carjack_throw.description: How a driver the hero pulls out of a car goes down (jack_pull.gd; needs carjack and hit_feel: with hit_feel off, or this flag off, the driver's fall is the old 0.5 s drag and 1.8 m knock-down, resting 2.1 m from the sill, as ever): a grab and a pull-out, nobody launched. The hero's own part (jack_hold.gd, with this flag and hit_feel) is four beats read from the driver, about 1.8 to 2 s from the first reach to the step into the opening: he steps to a spot a little behind the driver's seat and beside the door, crouches and leans in, and takes hold with both hands (the left or the right on the collar, the upper chest below the neck, the other on the near upper arm, read each frame off the driver's skeleton, the palms turned to the body and the fists closed on it; reach, 0.5 s, longer until both hands are on); holds on bracing back while the driver sits up and leans against it (struggle, 0.4 s); pulls (the driver is drawn out, the hands on them, the hero bent forward over them, following the collar out and a little toward the car's rear (a stride and a half: 3.7 to 3.9 m/s at the most over a tenth of a second, a van 4.4) and giving way where the body swings out through where he stands, until they are let go beside the door); and lets go (the hands ease out over 0.25 s, they never jump; at any sim speed the street is held at real time from the hero's reach until the driver has got up (4x and 8x change nothing about the pull: 0.68 s of wall time from the blow to the let-go at 8x and at 1x), and a hero knocked down mid-reach or mid-pull lets go of the car at once, the driver left where they are or on the road, the hero where he fell). His hands never rise above his own head. The door camera looks from the front quarter, above the door, and pushes in slowly during the pull. He steps into the opening and jogs in to take the seat (climbing in about 1.9 s after the pull, hands on the wheel about 3.2 s after it: the climb in is the car_in clip's own 1.3 s). The driver is dragged out of the seat sideways over the sill in the sit pose (0.7 s, speeding up, facing as they sat, leaning to the door and back, their hips coming down with the tip once over the sill), let go beside the door, slides a little further and sits down on the road, falls back and lies there along the car's side (head to the rear, feet toward the front), then gets up and runs as ever: they rest 1.15 m from the sill (never past 1.2 m), no part of the body is ever more than 0.25 m over the road once out of the seat and none of its skin more than 0.22 m under it, their hips are above 0.25 m for only a moment (no arc, no flip, no spin, nobody leaves the ground, and the lying pose comes in without the body sinking into the road). They count as down (the hero cannot punch or photograph them) from the haul through the get-up, not through the shout and the run after it. A moving car carries them on at its pace (the haul all of it, easing down over its last 0.2 s to the pace the slide keeps, at most 5 m/s). A car beside the door (its nose or tail within about 1.8 m up or down the road of where they are let go, more for a moving car; not one ahead or behind in its lane), a wall, post or bystander shortens the drop (down to 0.2 m) so they come down in the gap (a gap under about 1.45 m between the cars has no room for a body: it comes down in the next car and is pressed back out, once even when it is off screen). The open driver's door, as far open as it hangs (its real outline, glass and frame included), is kept off the body: the point they are let go at is moved down the car's side as far as the door asks for the feet's reach (0.60 to 0.70 m for every car but the vans, 0.90 m for the vans; the body goes straight out over the sill first and drifts there from a quarter of the way across): no vertex of the skinned body goes through any of the 17 models' doors (the closest 0.026 m); the cost is a limb through the car's own rear side behind the door for a frame or two (up to 0.42 m). The camera shakes at the yank and, a little (0.06 to 0.15 trauma by the blow's strength, under half the yank's), as the driver's hips touch the road, where the fall thump sounds, at any sim speed. Off (this flag, or hit_feel): the hero's part is the old one too, not only the driver's fall: he turns to the seat, reaches in, drags them out 0.55 s in and shoves them clear with the push clip, and steps into the opening at 1.3 s, all as before (a recorded door flow at a standstill matches the build before the pull-out frame for frame, but for the hero's grab, which is always the one above). Known limit: on an SUV or a van the open door panel covers about half the door camera's frame for the first 0.3 to 0.4 s of the grab (a higher view that cleared it broke the 5 degree hero-collar separation of fp_jack_grip_test).

police_response.description: The police answer the hero's offence in first person (traffic's police_response.gd): a police car called by a carjack, a knock-down or the third punch posts "Police arrived on <street>" at the scene and puts two officers out beside it (the roster's police bodies), who stand by the car and look for the hero. A hero on foot, or sitting in a stopped car, within 60 m gets one walking up, who shouts "Stop right there!" from 12 m (a hero standing at the car, or in a stopped car beside it, is shouted at first); a hero within 3 m of an officer for 2 s after the shout (or in a stopped car beside the police car) is busted: a toast "Busted: fined $500 for carjacking" ($200 for assault, $300 for a blow at an officer; the hero has no wallet, so it is the message and the witnesses' mood), a short fade, out of the car and put outside the nearest police station (where they stand with none), and the crew leaves early. The officers' timing is in real seconds (4x and 8x change nothing). A hero beyond 60 m, or driving off, has the officers back in the car and the car after them ("Police are after you", said once it is up to speed; its own lanes and speed, siren on, never placed and never blocking the hero) for 30 s, up to 60 s against a hero who has stopped while it closes or while it is within 40 m of them, before "Police lost you" ("Police gave up the chase" within 40 m); a car that gets as near as the roads go to a hero off them, or stands 5 s in the traffic, puts its officers out again from there (up to 60 m); a hero within 500 m when the car arrives is hunted at once, one beyond it is "No sign of the suspect". Off: a called car just sits at the scene with its siren for its stay, as before.

action_hijack.description: Action hijacks: driving alongside a moving car with someone at its wheel (within 2.5 m of its side, heading the same way at a similar speed, at least 4 m/s), F lets go of the wheel and the hero climbs out onto the roof, leaps across onto the other car, swings down to its driver's window, where he hangs on with a hand on the driver while the driver stands on the brakes (6 m/s^2) and the car pulls up. Nobody is pulled out of a moving car and the hero never takes the wheel without the pull: once the car stands still (a car still moving 2.5 s after the landing is stopped on the spot) and the car he left, rolling on beside it, is clear of the door (at most 3.5 s), he drops to the road beside the door and the rest is the stopped car's grab and two-hand pull (carjack, carjack_throw): the driver is struck down with the car at rest and the hero is seated at least 1 s after the blow, about 6 s on foot from the landing. A car that can no longer be taken (it pulled in to park, is gone or far) lets him drop to the road on foot, at once when it is gone and after 7 s at the window when it is not. The car left rolls on with nobody at the wheel, slowing as a car in neutral does, until it stops or hits something. Needs the carjack flag. Off: F at speed only says to slow down.

phone.description: First-person feature: B opens the phone Build app, which places roads, zones and buildings for the mayor who owns the land.

activity.description: First-person feature: AI activity feed, decision beacons and map pings showing which mayor or agent decided what, on which model, from which source, and where; mayors take staggered turns through the day on foot. J cycles the feed, G routes to the newest decision.

crews.description: First-person feature: the player's two building crews. Phone orders are built in real time (2-5 minutes for a building) by crews you can watch on site, with a board and a HUD card counting down; later orders queue for a free crew.

props.description: First-person feature: street props the player's car (and, with prop_bumps, the hero on foot) knocks over. Bins, benches, planters, mailboxes, bike racks, parking meters, traffic cones, wheelie bins and cartons hit hard enough tumble off, come to rest and can be hit again; they stand up again out of sight. Slower hits and lamps, trees, bollards and hydrants hold like walls.

prop_bumps.description: The hero on foot knocks light street props about: running into a bin, traffic cone, wheelie bin or carton fast enough for its kind knocks it over, and a punch or shove with nobody in reach lands on the prop in front. The hero, people walking and traffic kick fallen props along, and a fallen prop skidding fast knocks into the props in its way. Off: only the player's car knocks props over.

street_clutter.description: Everyday clutter on the sidewalks, all of it knockable: three traffic cones at the curb in front of a construction site, a wheelie bin out at the curb of some homes and a carton or two by some shop doors. Off: only the street furniture.

actions.description: First-person feature: the hero's body actions. Left mouse (right trigger) throws a jab, a cross and a heavier hook in turn, R shoves and X (middle mouse) kicks; the guard (right mouse or left trigger held) is the fighting stance. People reel or go down, the street reacts and the city hears of it. Keys 1-5 wave, nod, shake the head, shout and dance, and the people around answer.

arena_ask.description: First-person feature and orbit Powers button: Ask the five. /ask <question> in the chat (or the Powers tab in orbit) sends one question to all five mayors' models at once, each from the same city state it plans a normal turn from, and a panel shows who answered first and how: finish order, thought, post, proposed orders in plain words and plausibility flags. Nothing is applied to the city (a what-if). Costs five extra live calls per ask when a key is in use; budgeted to 1 ask per 60 s and 5 per game day. Without a key, offline or with the breaker open each column shows that mayor's last recorded turn (tagged as not having heard the question) or the offline planner. The calls are isolated: they never touch the breaker, the caches or the saves.

reporter.description: First-person feature: the player as the Gazette's stringer. Every AI decision with a place is a lead: K takes one on assignment and sets a waypoint to the scene, a quote from someone there (a talk reply or the Ask someone here answer) and an optional press photo (photo mode, scene in the marks) make the story, and K files it into the chat for points and press ranks. L opens the mayors' league: the five mayors ranked, the press card, the open leads and the latest stories.

health.description: First-person feature: the hero's health, an arc round the left of the minimap. Crashes in the car the hero drives, hard landings, people who fight back and cars that cannot stop for the hero cost points, which come back a few seconds after the last hurt. A blow makes the hero flinch (the guard up takes most of a punch), a car or a bad fall knocks them down for a moment, and with nothing left they are knocked out: the screen goes black and they come round outside the nearest hospital, healed.

fight_back.description: Some of the people the hero punches or shoves (and does not knock down) fight back: they square up, close in and throw jabs and crosses that hurt the hero within reach, until the hero goes down, gets away or drives off, or they are knocked down. Needs the health feature. Off: everyone shouts, runs off or walks back.

hit_by_cars.description: A car in traffic that can no longer stop for the hero on foot runs them down instead of halting dead: it brakes hard, the hero is thrown along and knocked down (or out at speed). Needs the health feature. Off: every car stops short of the hero.

jcb.description: A yellow backhoe loader is parked at a rare share of the curb slots, and the player can get in and drive it like a car: slower (about 22 km/h) and heavier, its seat, wheel and pedals fitted to the hero. Off: no backhoes park in town.

backhoe_arm.description: At the backhoe's wheel the loader arm moves: Y raises it and U lowers it (a full sweep in about four seconds), I curls the bucket in and O tips it out, the angles holding where the keys let go; a backhoe left with its arm up stays that way. A dig — the bucket tipped out with O, then curled back in with I with the arm low, over a construction site — grows a dirt pile in front of the machine, which stays once the hero drives off and starts again wherever the next dig happens to be. The pose and the pile are saved: a load puts the arm back as the hero left it (the machine found by the curb slot it came from) and stands the pile where it was, its level kept. Off: the arm and bucket stay folded as shipped.

backhoe_work.description: A backhoe parked at a construction site works the site on its own: while the crew is clearing, excavating or grading, its loader arm and bucket cycle through a dig — the arm down, a curled scoop, the haul up, the dump — each site's sweep on its own phase, seeded from the site, the day and the city seed so a replay sees the same sweep. The hero stepping in takes the arm over where it visibly is, and the loop's own posing is never saved. Off: the parked machines sit with folded arms.

heavy_motors.description: The hero can take the wheel of the town's working vehicles once they have nearly stopped: a bus at its stop, a garbage truck or a delivery truck held up in traffic (its driver pulled out first, as any carjack: the cab has no door that opens, so the hero reaches in from the side, takes hold of the driver and pulls them down out of it, and takes the wheel once they are out). Each drives like itself — a bus tops out around 78 km/h and lumbers up to it, a garbage truck is slower still, a delivery truck a little brisker, and all of them steer on a shorter lock and take longer to pull up, besides weighing as much as their kind does (a bus six sedans, a truck four), and they shove what they hit as heavy as they are: a bus runs a stopped car down the road and rolls on. Off: only cars and the backhoe.

bike_ride.description: The hero can get on a bicycle a cyclist has nearly stopped (the rider is pulled off first with the carjack flag, taken by the collar and the arm and put down on the road beside it as a driver is; with it off they are left standing beside it). It rides like itself — about 25 km/h flat out, quick off the mark, turning far tighter than any car and pulling up short, and it weighs almost nothing, so a car barely feels the knock. The hero sits on the saddle, hands on the grips and feet on the pedals, which the cranks carry round under them as they ride. Off: bicycles are traffic only.

class_audio.description: Each vehicle class speaks in its own voice: lorries, buses and emergency motors sound a deep air horn and a diesel chug, scooters a thin buzz and a two-stroke whine, and a bicycle's bell is a real bell (it used to borrow the car horn; a cyclist stuck in a jam used to honk one too). A held press on H leans on the long horn, not only the street's reaction to it. Off: every horn and engine is the car's, as before.

scooters.description: Step-through scooters in the street: about one in twelve of the unnamed vehicles is one (a commuter at about 35 km/h, filtering through gaps a car cannot, like the cyclists), and one stands at a share of the filled curb slots. The hero can step onto one that has nearly stopped (no door; its rider is pulled off first with the carjack flag, as a driver is) and ride it: about 45 km/h flat out, quicker off the mark than a bicycle, turning nearly as tight, hands on the grips and feet on the floorboard with a slight forward lean, and a horn, not a bell. Off: no scooters anywhere.

night_driving.description: Night driving: after dark the car the hero drives always throws its own headlight beam — a dedicated lamp beside the street's shared pool — and a bicycle a small dim lamp at its handlebar; and H at the wheel sounds the horn (a bicycle's bell), which the street hears through its own horn source. Off: after dark the car the hero drives shares the street's lamp pool like any other, and H does nothing at the wheel.

blocked_horns.description: A car the hero has held up — their car stopped in the lane ahead of it, or the hero on foot in the road — honks at them within a couple of seconds (leaning on it the longer they are held), instead of waiting on the long jam draw that rarely fires. Off: horns come only from long jams.

overtaking.description: Overtaking: a car stuck behind an inherently slow vehicle — a backhoe-paced machine, a bus or a truck with its own low top speed — swings through the opposing lane and past it when that lane is clear, then back; never inside a junction, at a stop line, beside parked cars, or to leapfrog a queue. Off: everyone queues behind the slowest.

traffic_lazy_tilebuilt.description: A built or cleared tile's lane-graph rebuild (lanes, crossings, junction props, vehicle smoothing) waits and runs a couple of tiles per traffic step instead of inside CityView's build frame, so a burst of rebuilt tiles spreads over the frames that follow. Off: every tile rebuilds its lanes inside the tile_built signal, all in the building frame.

horn_reach.description: The horn reaches the street: a car stopped or crawling ahead of the car the hero drives — held up by a conversation, stunned by a knock, or sitting where it ran someone down — shakes it off and gets going when the hero sounds the horn within about 15 m of it (a bicycle's bell does not). Off: the horn is only heard.

horn_street.description: The street hears the hero's horn: each sounding of the car's horn is put on the bus with where it sounds from and how far it carries (about 35 m), a held press leaning on it long, for the people and the birds round about to answer. A bicycle's bell carries nothing. Off: the horn sounds but nothing is told of it.

parkour.description: First-person feature: Space in front of an obstacle gets the hero over it instead of jumping against it. A railing, a bench or a low wall (up to 1.1 m tall and 0.9 m deep, with room to land beyond) is vaulted, a ledge up to 0.7 m hopped onto and one up to 2.1 m climbed, the climb clip playing as the body pulls itself up. Off: Space always jumps.

wall_climb.description: Space at a wall taller than the parkour climb (a building's side) takes hold of it: the hero leaps onto it and climbs it with the move keys (Shift faster), hands and feet on holds, climbs over the top where there is room to stand and steps off at its foot. Crouch lets go, Space pushes off. Needs the parkour feature. Off: Space jumps at such a wall.

landing_roll.description: A hard landing on the move (a drop of about 1.8 m to 10 m, moving at 1 m/s or more) rolls the hero on along the ground over a shoulder, and they come up moving on: the fall costs much less health and never knocks them down. A wall or a drop right ahead leaves an ordinary landing. Needs the parkour feature. Off: every hard landing hurts in full.

free_running.description: Free running at a sprint: Shift held on a straight run builds up over about a second to a sprint of 6.5 m/s (a run is 4.5 m/s). At that pace a low obstacle just ahead is vaulted or hopped onto with no press, Space at a ledge up to 3 m runs up it and climbs over (2.1 m otherwise), an edge with ground across the gap that a running jump reaches is leapt, and coming down from a jump the hands catch a ledge just ahead and climb onto it. Needs the parkour feature. Off: Shift tops out at a run and every move needs Space.

momentum.description: The hero on foot moves with weight: getting up to a run takes about 0.7 s and pulling up from one about 1.2 m (a walk stays brisk), a run turns more slowly than a walk, and a hard turn at a run sheds pace until the body faces the new way. Off: the old brisk starts, stops and turns.

animals.description: First-person feature: dogs in the street. Some people walk a dog on a lead (residents whose household lives with a dog, unless they are off to work, and a share of everyone else, fewer at night and in the rain and more of them while the city is young), and a dog household keeps its dog in the front yard while nobody walks it. Dogs heel, sniff, roam round an owner who stops, come over to a crouching hero, bark at the hero and at passers-by, flinch at blows and shouts, leap clear of cars and defend an owner the hero hits, biting. E pets a dog close by.

pigeons.description: Flocks of pigeons in the street (part of the animals feature). By day, from first light to dusk, they forage on the sidewalk in front of some shops and of the civic buildings people gather at, in the parks, and on a share of the plain street corners; and where no such spot is near, one ambient flock keeps to the sidewalk by the player, so even a day-old city shows pigeons. Walking with the head's bob, pecking at the ground, a cock now and then puffing up to coo. They walk out of people's way and flutter off from the hero walking at them; a sprint, a blow, a shout, a dog close by, a crash or a car coming at them sends the whole flock up with a clatter of wings, to wheel round over the street and glide back down once it is calm. E throws them crumbs and they come in round the hero's feet. Off: no pigeons.

perched_birds.description: Pigeons on the high perches (part of the animals feature). By day a share of the street's lamps keeps a bird on the pole top, and a share of the built lots a row along the roof edge of its tallest block facing the street, from plain homes to the civic buildings. They sit, preen and turn on their perches above the passing street: people, cars and the hero below never stir them. A shout or a blow below, a dog barking or a crash sends them up with a clatter to wheel over the roofs and glide back onto their perches. Off: the pigeons keep to the ground.

waterfowl.description: Ducks on the water (part of the animals feature). By day a share of the river's and the ponds' open water keeps a flock of mallards, a drake or two among the hens: they paddle about their spot, tip tail-up to feed under the surface and preen their feathers with a shake of their wings. The hero wading in or walking down to the bank close by, a shout, a crash or a dog coming at the water sends the flock up with a clatter of wings — they run along the surface, climb away, wheel round over the water and glide back down to land once it is calm. By night they are gone, off to roost. Off: no ducks.

cats.description: Cats in the street (part of the animals feature). A share of the houses with a front yard (and no dog) keep a cat there and a share of the shops a shop cat by the door; by night strays come out by the works yards and in the parks, and in the rain they all stay in. A young city without any of those keeps one ambient stray about near the player instead, day or night. They sit, loaf, groom, sleep, stretch and stroll about; a friendly cat comes over to a crouching hero with its tail up, an aloof one walks off, a skittish one runs. A sprint, a blow or a shout makes them jump and run, a dog close by makes them arch and hiss, a car coming makes them bolt, and a hunter stalks the pigeons, crouches and pounces (the flock gets away). E pets a cat: it purrs, strolls off or hisses. Off: no cats.

squirrels.description: Squirrels on the lawn (part of the animals feature). By day a share of the woods that ring the city and of the trees in the street — a street tree, a lot's own — keeps a squirrel: it bounds about a patch of grass at the foot of its trunk, stops, sits up on its haunches to nibble with its paws at its mouth and sways its tail behind it. The hero walking up to it or sprinting near, a dog close by or running, a person stepping on it or a shout sends it chattering once and dashing for its tree, up the trunk to cling there head-up until the trouble has gone, then back down to its lawn. By night they are in their dreys. Off: no squirrels.

hit_feel.description: First-person feature: how blows feel. A blow of the hero's that lands freezes the world for a few hundredths of a second (hit-stop, longer for a harder blow or a knock-down) and shakes the camera; a blow on the hero, a crash and someone the player's car hits shake it too. Someone knocked down is thrown up off their feet, lands and bounces before they lie there (higher for a car). Off: blows only kick the view and knock-downs stay on the ground.

directional_hits.description: People stagger away from the side a blow lands on without turning to face it first. Harder blows lean them further and keep them off balance longer, and a heavy melee blow staggers them briefly before they fall. Throws and car hits still launch at once. Off: people turn toward every blow and always reel backward.

strike_recovery.description: A blow that lands on a person, animal or prop brings the hero's torso back into stance briskly. A swing at empty air follows through further and leaves a short extra recovery before the next attack, longer for a kick or hook. Throws, slams and counters keep their existing timing. Off: landed and missed strikes recover identically.

strike_step.description: A grounded punch or weapon swing at someone just inside its reach steps the hero in as it winds up: at most 18 cm in all, easing to a stop 95 cm short of them, and the world holds it as a walk does (never into a wall, a prop or another person). The blow's own reach never grows; kicks, shoves, throws and swings at empty air keep their feet. Off: every attack is thrown from where the hero stands.

melee.description: First-person feature: weapons to pick up. Baseball bats lie in the parks and by some homes, steel pipes on the sidewalk by industrial lots and bottles by shops. E by one picks it up (swapping for the one in hand), Z drops it, and getting into a car or being knocked down drops it too. In hand the strike button swings it, forehand and backhand, further and harder than a fist: a bat makes people reel, a pipe knocks them down and a bottle knocks them down and breaks in a spray of glass. Off: no weapons lie about.

animal_hits.description: A kick or a weapon swing of the hero's lands on the dog, cat or pigeon in front when no person is in reach (a fist goes over them). A dog yelps, is knocked back and flinches, then runs off whining, or turns on the hero if it is a barker and the blow was light; a cat yowls, is knocked back and bolts, wary of the hero from then on; a pigeon is knocked up and away in a puff of feathers and its flock takes off. A thump, a short hit-stop and a camera shake go with it. Off: kicks and swings go through the animals, as before.

brawl.description: First-person feature: grapples. H (or the back mouse button) takes hold of the person in front: they hang in the hero's hands, fists up, and are dragged along at a walk. Punches land on them where they hang (the hook or the third in a row floors them), R throws them where the camera looks (knocked down and flung about 3 m) and H again lets go; after six seconds they break free, then shout, fight back or walk off. Getting into a car or being knocked down lets go. Off: no grapples.

slams.description: Environmental attacks: R with someone held and something solid just beyond them (within 0.8 m of their body) slams them into it instead of throwing them. A bin, a traffic cone, a wheelie bin or a carton goes over with them and they go down over it; a wall, a post, a parked car or a heavier prop that holds (a bench, a mailbox, a planter) stops them dead and they drop off it to the side. A heavy thump, a longer hit-stop and a harder camera shake go with it. Off: R always throws.

counters.description: Counters: someone fighting the hero who starts a punch flashes a red cue above their head, and the guard raised (right mouse) in the moment before it lands counters it: the punch misses and the hero's hook knocks them down. A guard held up since earlier only blocks, as before. Off: the guard only ever blocks.

counter_cues.description: How a punch thrown at the hero reads. The fighter's wind-up holds back through the first half of the run to the punch, then snaps in at speed, the punch's own timing untouched; and the red counter mark above the attacker's head grows as the blow closes and fades away once it has landed. Off: the wind-up plays at one speed and the mark keeps the same size until it goes.

fight_tempers.description: People who fight back each fight their own way, fixed to who they are: one turns near half of the hero's blows aside on their guard (nothing moves them and nothing counts), one sidesteps round the hero while waiting to punch, one calls friends over and up to two join the scrap, one squares up but thinks better of it and runs, and a tough one leads with the cross and answers a blow the moment it lands. Needs the fight_back feature. Off: every one of them fights the same, jab and cross at one pace.

weapon_disarm.description: A swing with a weapon that a guarded fighter (the guard temper, fight_tempers) turns aside never lands: no weapon_hit, a bottle stays whole — and some of those turn-asides (DISARM_ODDS, about a third, rolled on the fighter and the scrap, never the shared roll) knock the weapon from the hero's hand, flying a metre off to lie there and be picked up again. Off: the swing is wasted but the weapon stays.

fight_seeded_rolls.description: Reaction outcomes roll off the sim seed and who the person is, not off the shared reaction stream: whether someone shoved or punched fights back, and whether a guarded brawler turns a blow aside (fight_back, fight_tempers) are hashed from the seed, the walker's id and their resident id (the guard's roll salts with the blow's own count, so the share turned aside still varies blow to blow), and which onlooker jeers a ringed brawl picks off the same hash (brawl_ring), so the answer is the same however many unrelated reactions ran first. Off: those rolls and the jeer pick draw from the shared stream in reaction order, as before.

brawl_ring.description: A brawl with three or more in it forms a ring: the first two to square up engage the hero as ever, the rest hold two metres out on their own ray from the fight, facing in and punching nothing, until a slot ahead opens — one down or out of the scrap — and they step in. The crowd round the ring jeers, one turning to shout every breath or two. Off: every fighter piles in at once and the crowd keeps its own counsel.

shake_wobble_clamp.description: Camera shake at low frame rates: the wobble's fastest line (~15.6 Hz) is capped to under 4 samples a frame (the smoothed frame interval paces it), so at 20-25 fps the shake swings slower but coherently instead of jumping pseudo-randomly past Nyquist. 60 fps never reaches the cap. Off: the shake always runs at full speed.

down_view.description: Knocked down in first person, the view goes with the body: the eye sinks toward the ground through the fall, lies flat tipped a little up to the sky (and whoever stands over the hero), and comes back up with the get-up — driven by the knock-down's own phases, so control still returns exactly when the get-up ends. Third person reads the body's anim as before. Off: the view stays at standing height while down.

hit_direction.description: In first person, a blow that lands flashes a short red arc on the screen's edge toward the side it came from, beside the vignette's flash, fading over half a second (hit_wedge.gd in the health screen), and the hurt's thump pans the same way (hero_hit_dir; the audio feature). You always know where it came from without reading the flinch. Off, and always in third person: no marker, no pan.

hero_flinch.description: How a blow that lands on the hero reads. The body flinches the way the blow came from — one in the face snaps the head back, one in the back or the side folds the chest — and the camera rolls toward the side that was hit, harder for a harder blow while hit_feel is on (with it off the jolt keeps one size). Needs the health feature. Off: every flinch is the same fixed jolt, the two flinch clips alternating.

downed_awareness.description: The street answers a body on the ground. A blow that leaves someone down brings the nearest onlooker within six metres over to them: they walk up beside the body, lean in with a slow head shake a moment, then walk on — once for each knock-down, and never one of the fight's own. And a fighter whose blows put the hero down stands over them a beat — one last shout — before walking off. Off: nobody comes to look, and a fighter who downs the hero walks off the same instant.

crowd_gasp.description: The crowd gasps when someone goes down in view: the onlookers who stay (not the ones who run) rock back as one — no beat of looking first, a sharp backward tip before they shout. Once per crowd: another body falling within six seconds and ten metres of the last gets the plain reaction. Visual only; there is no gasp clip in the sounds bank. Off: onlookers take their usual moment, then shout or run as before.

guard_break.description: A brawler's beaten guard staggers open. When chipping (guard_chip) wears through the guard of a brawler who turns the hero's blows aside (fight_tempers), it drops: the fighter reels off balance for a beat — throwing no punches, turning nothing aside, every blow landing — until the guard knits back whole and can be chipped anew. Off: a beaten guard just fails, every later blow landing, with no stagger and no recovery.

throw_impact.description: A thrown or flung body bounces off what it meets mid-flight. Someone thrown (the brawl throw) whose arc meets a wall or a solid prop stops short against it with a short rebound off the face and slumps where they come to rest, instead of halting dead in the air or sliding along it. The throw's one person_hit carries the predicted impact in its info ("impact": {"at", "in"}), so audio can land the second thump; there is no second emission. Off: the flight stops dead at the wall as before.

guard_chip.description: Guards wear out. Punches the hero's guard catches drain its poise (a sliver inside the health arc) until the guard breaks: that blow lands in full, the guard drops and the hero staggers a beat, the view dipped; the poise knits back once the blows stop. And a brawler who turns the hero's blows aside (fight_tempers) has their own guard chipped the same way, until one lands in full. Off: guards never tire, as before.

low_vram_auto.description: Low-GPU-memory mode picks itself on an integrated GPU, a card with 4 GB or less, or one with under 1.5 GB free at startup (another program holding the rest): smaller shadow maps, FXAA instead of MSAA, lighter SSAO, and first person starts on the Low preset until the player saves one. GRIDFALL_LOW_VRAM=1 or 0 forces it either way. Off: only GRIDFALL_LOW_VRAM=1 turns it on.

gmi_live.description: Kill switch for live GMI Cloud calls. Off: every call uses the replay cache or heuristics, as with GRIDFALL_OFFLINE=1.

gmi_web_safe_headers.description: Web build only (desktop is unchanged): send live GMI requests with just the Authorization and Content-Type headers. A browser must clear a CORS preflight before every call, and GMI's answer (measured 2026-11-03: OPTIONS /v1/chat/completions allows Content-Type, Authorization, X-Requested-With and x-gmi-request-id) does not list User-Agent, X-Request-ID or X-Trace-ID, which the client otherwise sends, so with them every browser call is blocked and the game quietly runs on the replay cache. The request and trace ids still label each call in the local GMI Log and trace; only the wire headers change. Switch it off if GMI's CORS allow-list ever admits those headers (tools/demo_check.sh prints the current Allow-Headers).

replay_horizon.description: The recorded replay cache (data/gmi_replay_cache.json, one captured game of 12 days) answers a key only up to the last day recorded for it. Past that the call falls through to the scripted planner (source heuristic), so an offline or keyless city at day 14 no longer replays day 12 forever (the same sewage burst at the same tile, the same headline, the same mayor posts). This session's own live answers have no horizon. Off: the nearest recorded day answers at any day, as before.

gmi_preflight.description: Once per key, in the real game (not in tests), one GET of the GMI model list (through GmiClient, with just the Authorization and Content-Type headers) compared with the 14 model ids the game calls. The key panel then says '13 of 14 models available; Mei Kimura will use the offline planner' and the GMI log gets one line. Never without a key, under GRIDFALL_OFFLINE=1 or with gmi_live off; it leaves the breakers and counters alone. Off: no model list is read.

gmi_inflight_cap.description: Caps the background GMI calls (the residents' batches, the street chatter and the talk) at 6 at once, 3 while a mayor, a support agent or an Ask-the-five call is out; the mayors and support agents never wait. For a key whose tier rate-limits a burst or a browser that queues requests: turn it on if the GMI log shows 429s at dawn. Off by default because it delays the residents' plans, and the day gate waits for them in the Planner (up to 75 s).

frame_dt_clamp.description: A frame longer than 1 s (a browser tab that was hidden for minutes, a window dragged, a long hitch) advances the street's traffic, animals, weather and the Planner's walkers by at most 1 s of real time (Pacing.frame_dt), so the street's traffic is not worked off in one frame (measured: a 600 s frame at 8x replaced every moving car of the test street; clamped, none moved more than 100 m) and nothing fast-forwards at 8x. The sim clock was already bounded by its backlog clamp. Off: the raw frame delta, as before.

visibility_autosave.description: Web only: when the browser tab is hidden, the city autosaves once (the morning autosave rule applies: not within 60 s of the last save, flag autosave_gap). A closed tab never reaches the quit autosave, and a hidden tab is how most of them are closed. Off: only the morning autosave persists a web session.

player_gmi_key.description: The pause menu's GMI Cloud page, where a player pastes their own GMI API key to run the mayors live (the web build's bring-your-own-key). The key lives in memory for the session and, on the web and only after they tick Remember on this device, in their browser's localStorage; it is never logged. Off: the page is hidden and no key can be entered in-game.

analytics.description: Local product analytics to user://ops/analytics.jsonl (also GRIDFALL_ANALYTICS=1). Nothing is sent anywhere.

error_tracking.description: Write contextual error records to user://ops/errors.jsonl (also GRIDFALL_ERROR_LOG=1). In-memory error counters are always on.

web_first_use_marks.description: Web only, local console: first-use marks and stopwatches for the probe kit (scripts/ops/first_use.gd). A FIRSTUSE console line and a User Timing mark at the first sight of the lamp pool, a headlight beam, the overview, the pause menu, a beacon, a construction site, a poster composite and rain, and a stopwatch around the first play() of each audio stream and the save's stringify and file write; every 10 s an AUDIOSEC line with the slowest frame of each audio section (scripts/fp/audio/audio_feature.gd). Nothing leaves the browser. Off by default; a probe run turns it on through user://feature_flags.json (tools/web_fps_probe.js, GF_FPS_FLAGS).

day_drain_fast.description: At 4x and 8x the sliced sim runs extra day-start pieces (the brain's day round and the residents' plan batches, one per frame at 1x and 2x) in the frame within a wall-clock budget (SpreadDrain.BUDGET_MS, 8 ms) that counts the pieces the per-frame paths run anyway, and what the drain spends comes out of the pump's share of the frame. A frame already full of pieces (a piece of 5 ms or more in the browser, two sources) gets none, so no frame is longer than without it. The clock waits fewer frames at dawn only where pieces are cheap (native: 1 to 2 ms); a browser gain is not demonstrated. Same pieces in the same order: pacing only. Off: one piece per frame at every speed.

warmup_orbit_variants.description: Web only: the shader warm-up groups the scene's materials by shader variant instead of raw recipe (a grown city is covered inside the same time budget), draws them from the stage alone (isolated camera and sun), adds the Planner's own materials (data/warm_orbit_variants.json) and runs the states prototypes, Tab overview, no-shadow and street. Off: the recipe-per-material warm-up of before, with the states prototypes and one unlit+noshadow list, no isolated stage, no Planner catalogue, and a scene with more than 600 distinct materials is not warmed. (The work-based progress percentage and the loader's stripe are not behind this flag.)

planner_prepare_overlay.description: Web only: every move up to the Planner view and every Tab back to the street shows a Preparing the Planner / Back to the street overlay (HTML, painted before the heavy frame, the world held still) and keeps it up after the move until five frames in a row take under 50 ms (at most 6 s), instead of a frozen picture and bare freezes after it. It does not shorten the wait: the move still freezes about 2 to 4 s. The Planner's own shader warm-up behind it is opt-in (planner_warm in user://warmup_tuning.json) and measured not to pay. Off: the view switches at once (and the browser freezes while it links its shader programs).

ops_alerts.description: Evaluate data/alert_rules.json and print OPS_ALERT lines. Player toasts additionally need GRIDFALL_OPS_ALERTS_UI=1.
